steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: I'm starving...

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: (Sniffs) That smells amazing!

steps.name: Dirt-Poor Peddler
steps.text: Hey, have you heard the news?

steps.name: Dirt-Poor Peddler
steps.text: The Druid's Treasure! Everyone's going mad about it!

steps.name: Skint Peddler
steps.text: Can't be stuffed, can't be bothered, don't care.

steps.name: Skint Peddler
steps.text: If there is treasure, it goes to the upper crust. Not gonna make its way to us, is it?

steps.name: Dirt-Poor Peddler
steps.text: Who says not?

steps.name: Dirt-Poor Peddler
steps.text: Oh, you think this is just our lot, eh? We deserve this?

steps.name: Skint Peddler
steps.text: Look, forget that...

steps.name: Skint Peddler
steps.text: Someone's making off with your stuff.

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: (Treasure... my bruv's looking for that, right?)

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: (Okay, while the man's distracted...)

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: (Ow, hot!)

steps.name: Dirt-Poor Peddler
steps.text: Hey!

steps.name: Dirt-Poor Peddler
steps.text: Trying to steal from me?!

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: Krgh!

steps.name: Dirt-Poor Peddler
steps.text: Bloody runt! Don't you dare muss up my stand!

steps.name: Dirt-Poor Peddler
steps.text: Get back here!

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: How are your injuries?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: They're doing fine.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: No word from the Doctor still?

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: Contact with them's been lost ever since they entered Londinium. All means of communication so far are kaput.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: What about your end?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: We've disseminated the news out.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: At the very least right now, no matter how many believe it, the Duke's people are letting us have the pretense of an investigation in order to station at the duchy's north border.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: If it all holds, we can come to the Doctor's rescue at any time.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: Hm... alright, good.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: For now, let's get these intel notes to the landship.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: The Doctor's group will be fine.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: They will.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: Right, the children at the refugee camp...

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Bring them here.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: It's... safer for them here.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: Susie wants you.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: I'll be off.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Susie, didn't I tell you to get some proper rest first?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: I can cope here. I don't need help with anything, really.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: What's wrong? What has you so unhappy?

steps.name: Goldenglow
steps.text: The streets here, the city... everything's changed so much.

steps.name: Goldenglow
steps.text: I've never seen so many of the Guards out and about before.

steps.name: Goldenglow
steps.text: Everyone's rushing everywhere. We all look so tense.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Nobody knows what the situation in Londinium is like right now.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: We have people escaping out here one after another, with nothing but scraps of testimonies and info contradicting info.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: It's become the source of panic and rumor in its own right.

steps.name: Goldenglow
steps.text: I know what's happening. You don't have to hide it from me, Quercus.

steps.name: Goldenglow
steps.text: Everyone's busy right now... I want to help too.

steps.name: Goldenglow
steps.text: Grani wouldn't even tell me about you and the refugees at first.

steps.name: Goldenglow
steps.text: I know... you're all looking out for me.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: You're a kind girl, Susie. That's why.

steps.name: Goldenglow
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Look, see the marks left on this leaf—bug-eaten, sun-bleached.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Everything that's happening right now will be figured out.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: No matter if it's me, Grani, or anyone else who does it.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: No matter if it turns out well or not.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: And most people will forget it ever happened before long.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: But the ones who've been through it won't. Some marks are left forever.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: So...

steps.name: Goldenglow
steps.text: Listen, I'm not a child anymore!

steps.name: Goldenglow
steps.text: Quercus!

steps.name: Goldenglow
steps.text: Look, I made this bread myself, I learned how to do it aboard Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Goldenglow
steps.text: You always used to have to make me snacks, Quercus...

steps.name: Goldenglow
steps.text: So... I want to help you.

steps.name: Goldenglow
steps.text: Help everyone.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Oh, but still, it'll sting.

steps.name: Goldenglow
steps.text: Eh?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Sting our little Susie, and Grani, and those children.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: You'll find nothing in the refugee camp but cries of distress, sighs of despair, and howls of longing.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: I've given everything I have to ward the haze of sickness from people, purely because they wouldn't resign themselves to death, because in their heart still laid cares.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Some have calmly accepted the end of their life, and I've accompanied them in their final moments, in their tranquil return to the earth.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: But the endless spread of pestilence is drying and crumbling the soil beneath us, rendering it rough and unyielding.

steps.name: Goldenglow
steps.text: And that's why you want them to get the children out, and bring them here?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Yes...

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: All that takes place there is far too stifling for the newborn saplings.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: But that said...

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: I've never doubted your ability nor your courage, Susie.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: So long as you're willing, you can come spend time with the children here from now on.

steps.name: Goldenglow
steps.text: Mm-hm!

steps.name: Goldenglow
steps.text: Also!

steps.name: Goldenglow
steps.text: I'm not a child anymore!

steps.name: Goldenglow
steps.text: And you're... so amazing, Quercus! You can use Arts to make withered plants regrow.

steps.name: Goldenglow
steps.text: Everything will get better.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Arts are no panacea, you know.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Take that frail, sickly sapling, for instance.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: The one in the corner.
On an evening in early autumn, Quercus is quietly stood in the garden, listening in stillness.
The souls are mournful, their cry as clear as ever on the wind.

steps.name: Haze
steps.text: Well, meow...

steps.name: Haze
steps.text: I have to say, this is my first time seeing the Druid's Arts.

steps.name: Goldenglow
steps.text: Wuh! When did you get here, Haze?

steps.name: Haze
steps.text: Oh, I didn't. I've been here.

steps.name: Haze
steps.text: They say the Druid can hear what the trees make conversation over.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: It's not conversation.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: It's the passing on of emotions, between souls, through the roots that connect life and the earth.
Quercus softly chants an age-old incantation, Arts like stars falling down upon the mundane nature we inhabit, imparting themselves upon the earth.
In a bout of fierce tremors, a sapling ruptures through the ground, its finest form unfolding itself towards the vastness of the sky.
Atop the branches burst forth fresh buds, telling of the call that summons new life.

steps.name: Goldenglow
steps.text: Wow!

steps.name: Goldenglow
steps.text: It just grew in an instant!

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Indeed.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: In an instant.

steps.name: Goldenglow
steps.text: Wait!

steps.name: Goldenglow
steps.text: Quercus! The... the tree!

steps.name: Goldenglow
steps.text: There's a child growing out of the tree!

steps.text: Once we find the Treasure, we want 60%.

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: 30% each for me and my little brother.

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: You want me to work, that's the price. No negotiations.

steps.name: Diminutive Mercenary
steps.text: Look how greedy the legendary Bent's gotten.

steps.name: Diminutive Mercenary
steps.text: Getting too big for your britches, I bet.

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: Alright. You want to go?

steps.name: Diminutive Mercenary
steps.text: If you think we're actually scared of you, you can dream on.

steps.name: Diminutive Mercenary
steps.text: Guh!

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: Got the guts to say that to me again?

steps.name: Diminutive Mercenary
steps.text: 30%, alright, you said it, 30%.

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: Each.

steps.name: Diminutive Mercenary
steps.text: Oh, no, yeah, yeah!

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: Now shove it.

steps.name: Diminutive Mercenary
steps.text: Right...

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: Wait. Any of you lot seen where my brother's about?

steps.name: Diminutive Mercenary
steps.text: Er...

steps.name: Diminutive Mercenary
steps.text: Saw the kid earlier at one of those stands nearby.

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: Carefree little bugger! I said for him not to run off!

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: Every single day with this! He drives me up the wall!

steps.name: Diminutive Mercenary
steps.text: Hey!

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Still hiding?

steps.text: Little rascal.

steps.text: Oi!

steps.text: Let me down!

steps.text: Oh! I wonder who your family is.

steps.text: Let... Let me get you down now.

steps.text: Careful...

steps.text: Augh!

steps.text: Don't... Don't steal my bread!

steps.text: What's gotten into you?!

steps.text: Hey! Here, you!

steps.text: (This bread's delish...)

steps.text: Wait, that's right!

steps.text: You were just talking about the Druid, weren't you!

steps.text: Even if I did...

steps.text: Because that's how it works.

steps.text: Then I'll tell my brother! I'll get him to ask you.

steps.text: He's right tough!

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: Super! Super! Super tough!!!

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: I'm not scared of you, okay!

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: That's right! I can cast stuff!

steps.text: I'm not as good as my brother, but you won't pick on me so easy!

steps.text: You think you're so mighty, don't you?

steps.text: What are you up to?!

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Hmph.
Countless vines drop down from the tree above her, and the feeble child is fastened sturdily in place before he can even react.
He resembles a startled cub in the moment, gnashing as he struggles to flail.

steps.text: Oi!

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: What are you doing?!

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Spanking you.

steps.name: Quercus

steps.text: Augh!

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: *whimper*...

steps.name: Emaciated Child

steps.text: But my brother does it too!

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: His Arts...

steps.text: Your brother?

steps.text: Oi! That's my stuff!

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: Damn you! Give it back!

steps.text: I found all that!

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Understand?

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: ...I'm not scared!

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: My brother... My brother says this way nobody'll pick on me!

steps.name: Emaciated Child

steps.name: Quercus

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: If your brother is as strong as you say...

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Why would he send you to do any of this?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Are you sure your brother knows you're here?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: You didn't tell him you were heading out, did you?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: What if your brother never comes?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: What if... we leave you here? Will your brother really be able to find you?

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: (Sobbing) I...

steps.name: Goldenglow
steps.text: (Quercus, don't you think we've scared him a little too much?)

steps.name: Goldenglow
steps.text: (I mean, I know it's wrong to steal... child or not.)

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: (I think our little Susie's just as much a child, then.)

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: What if... we take you away from here?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: And you never see your brother again...

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: No!

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: Don't... I...

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: I want to stay with my brother.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Then be truthful with me.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Tell me why you stole this medicine, and why you're after the Druid's Treasure.

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: Because my brother wanted it...

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: He's the one who looked after me ever since we left Londinium... He said there was treasure in Gododdin, and we could make loads and loads of money, and live happy days.

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: He's seriously, seriously strong! Nobody's ever been able to pick on us!

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: But he's been having worse and worse health, I can tell that... He's always using these medicines in secret.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: This kind?

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: I dunno. But it looks a lot like it.

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: I'm not a kid anymore.

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: I want to help my brother and all...

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: If I can find the treasure, and some medicine!

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: Then that'll make my brother super duper happy!

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: So...

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: Please, Miss.

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: Can you...

steps.text: I understand.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: But still, I can't tell you right this moment.

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: Oh...

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: Then... Then what do I have to do, before you tell me?

steps.text: I'm just here to check if you have everything all in place and sorted.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: I'll have Grani accompany the kids over.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Everything's ready.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: That kid in the garden...

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: You have some amazing patience.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: I'm only a doctor.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: I don't accede to every whim. I'm no fairy godmother.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: *sigh*... He's had a hard lot in life.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: We don't even know how his brother is.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: That's why I sent Susie back for now.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: She's too kind...

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: And as you meet each refugee in the camp, and every child that's sent here... you find each and every story tugs at your heart, doesn't it?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: That's why little Susie's the one I'm more worried for, really.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: And how are you going to explain the Druid's Treasure to him, then?

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: All it is is the cover we operate under. You know that.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: Not to mention we've still not heard a peep from the Doctor's end. We can't expose this.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: We have to prioritize Rhodes Island and our mission.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: So...

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: We give him a false goal, one that can never be achieved?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Make him chase fruitlessly, cluelessly, for the rest of his days?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: A sacrifice?

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: A sacrifice?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: I just feel...

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: It's not how Rhodes Island would do things.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: We can't just absolve ourselves of our actions like that.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: What are you going to do?!

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: Quercus, stop right there!

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: Explain.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Don't worry. I won't do anything to hurt Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: Oi!

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: Question for you. Seen a kid about this tall?

steps.name: Dirt-Poor Peddler
steps.text: The hell do you think you're doing?!

steps.name: Dirt-Poor Peddler
steps.text: Bloody hell! It was that little bastard just now! Your brother, I reckon, you look like two peas in a pod!

steps.name: Dirt-Poor Peddler
steps.text: Here I was narked I'd have no one to pay damages...

steps.name: Dirt-Poor Peddler
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: Where is he?!
The weak, frail figure of a child busies about the garden.

steps.text: Miss Quercus! I watered all the trees in the garden!

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: (It's only a momentary drive.)

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: I swept the path over there all nice and clean too!

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: (He may well be worn out any second now.)

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: What else do I need to do?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: (He throws himself dim-wittedly at everything without even knowing what this treasure is.)

spans.text: (He throws himself dim-wittedly at everything without even knowing what this treasure

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Do you know why I'm having you do these things?

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: Nope.

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: That one mister says it's because I've done bad things.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: And have you?

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: I don't know...

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: My brother's always done it. He says other people owe us all this stuff.

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: It's stuff we're meant to have.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: (The branches that rot are bade to be pruned.)

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: (The trunks that are gnawed are bade to be sawed.)

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Let me put it this way, then.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: You did something that ended with you being caught, and you put your brother through the hassle of saving you.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Was that bad of you?

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: ...Mm-hm.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: So if your brother gets hurt while saving you...

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Possibly... even worse.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Is that bad of you then?

steps.text: It is!

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Just as you cherish your brother, others have their own things, and their own people they cherish.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: If you take things as you see fit, then you'll make others angry, and get your brother into trouble in the end.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Understand?

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: Mm-hm...

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: I understand.

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: I won't do bad things anymore.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: (But who can say what form the treetop takes in this moment?)

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: (May life everlast.)

steps.text: Here?

steps.name: Dirt-Poor Peddler
steps.text: A... Around here...

steps.text: I chased him up to around here, and then, and then I lost him.

steps.name: Dirt-Poor Peddler
steps.text: Guh!

steps.text: Bent!

steps.text: You're here?!

steps.name: Emaciated Child
steps.text: Um!!

steps.text: I said for you not to run off!

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: I went through hell to scarper out with you! Every step of the way, you know how hard it's been?!

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: Don't you hang your head! I'm talking to you!

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: (Need me to help that kid out?)

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: (We can't leave him with someone like this, can we?)

steps.text: Who're you?

steps.text: Don't get in the way! Move it!

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: You're this child's elder brother?

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: And what's your business?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: 'Joe.' Is that your name?

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: Right, with me. We're going home.

steps.name: Joe
steps.text: I'm not going.

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: Can you just listen for once?!

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: You're stressing me out like this! Me, Mum and Dad, who do you think we've done everything for?

steps.name: Joe
steps.text: I'm not going.

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: You think I'm no use anymore, don't you? You think I can't provide for you, is it?!

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: Think you've outgrown the nest, don't need me looking after you?

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: Eh?!

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: Let me go!

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: This is not for an outsider like you to butt in. It's family business.

spans.text: for an outsider like you to butt in. It's family business.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: (Bitter Root.)

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: (Take the child aside.)

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: What are you doing?

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: Argh!

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: Urgh!

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: You let me go!

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Are we clear? I could easily dispose of you right now.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: And even your little brother.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: All because of how reckless you've been.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: You make me angry.

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: You!!

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: Argh!

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Quiet!

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Will you listen properly now?

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: Mmrgh...

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: I can put up with your insolence.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: It's not as if I don't respect all you've done for the child.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: I imagine you know the state of your infection all too well. Do you want to see the child end up the same way?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Was it you who taught him to use Arts to defend himself?

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: I had no other choice. It's the only thing they fear.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: And do you see fear in me?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: What if I killed the two of you right here and now?

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: You wouldn't dare!

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: I'd take you with me!

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: So you don't intend on surviving?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: What about your brother, then?

steps.name: Bent
steps.text: What is it you want?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: It's a secret between me and him.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: I won't allow you to take him until he fulfils his agreement with me.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: You can go back to your current dwellings and wait for him.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Of course, my people can find you at any time.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Or you could go to the refugee camp on the east end. They'll offer you help there.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Is my point clear?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: See?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: It turns out we can have a proper conversation.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: Argh!

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: Hey! Watch it, boy!

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: You're biting the hand that feeds you.

steps.name: Joe
steps.text: Miss Quercus!

steps.name: Joe
steps.text: Let my brother go!

steps.name: Joe
steps.text: He's a good person!

steps.name: Joe
steps.text: He's the best in all the land!

steps.name: Joe
steps.text: So I won't let you hurt him!

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: How am I the villain now?

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: The boy's got real strength when it counts...

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Joe, do you remember what you asked me about earlier on?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Be good and come with me now, and I'll tell you all you want to know.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: And I promise I won't hurt your brother, okay?

steps.name: Joe
steps.text: Okay!

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Now, do you think we're bad people?

steps.name: Joe
steps.text: If you and that mister pick on my brother, then yeah.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: So why didn't you use Arts just now to attack that mister, and save your brother?

steps.name: Joe
steps.text: Because you said using Arts would make the infection worse.

steps.name: Joe
steps.text: It's bad and it'll make my brother worry.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: So if I told you that you had to exchange your brother for the treasure, you wouldn't agree, would you?

steps.name: Joe
steps.text: I wouldn't do it, even if it was for treasure.

steps.name: Joe
steps.text: I would never... never ever!

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: (A life yet to bud grows with wild abandon.)

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Congratulations.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: You've passed the test.

steps.name: Joe
steps.text: What?!

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Only those who become Druids are qualified to find the Druid's Treasure.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: And you've successfully passed the first test.

steps.name: Joe
steps.text: Eh?

steps.name: Joe
steps.text: Becoming a Druid?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Indeed.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Come with me.

steps.name: Joe
steps.text: What's this place?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: This... is a place once holy to the Druids.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Only, the vast amount of time has made the legends hazy.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Here, age after age of tutor imparted the knowledge and the precepts upon the next generation.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Until the Druids began to die out, ever so gradually, in Victoria's history.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Joe, go and kneel upon the altar there.

steps.name: Joe
steps.text: Mm-hm.
Quercus snaps off cane from a tree, and flogs Joe across his back with force.
The searing pain forces him to bend over, upon which he immediately, stubbornly rights himself again.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Joe, young stray that you are.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: May the age-old faith be carved hardily into your heart. For all tribulation the future brings, shall your way forward never stray.
Quercus takes a berry from the bush, and with her thumb, draws a line of vivid red over the forehead of Joe.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: May the roots of the earth ever be bound with you. For however far you are separated from home, shall you never be lost nor hesitant.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: The branches that rot are bade to be pruned.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: The trunks that are gnawed are bade to be sawed.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: May life everlast.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Joe, I ask if you are willing to swear upon the ancient precepts, and become a true Druid.

steps.name: Joe
steps.text: I am.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Rise. From today forth, you are a Druid!

steps.name: Joe
steps.text: I'm a Druid now?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Mm. From here on, you must rely on yourself to seek the treasure of legend.

steps.name: Joe
steps.text: Have you found it then, Miss Quercus?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Not yet, no. I think... you'll find it before I do, perhaps.

steps.name: Joe
steps.text: Really?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Really.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: But you must keep it secret.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: For if you catch the eye of some very, very bad people, then they'll catch you, hurt you, and even hurt your brother.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Understand?

steps.name: Joe
steps.text: Mm-hm...

steps.name: Joe
steps.text: That's a bad thing. I won't do it.

steps.name: Joe
steps.text: So... can I tell my brother?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: What, you mean...

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: You wouldn't want to surprise him with something nice?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: See what I mean?

steps.name: Joe
steps.text: Oh...

steps.name: Joe
steps.text: Okay!

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: You're not honestly counting on a little kid to keep a secret, right?

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: How much danger will you bring on yourself if word of this gets out?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Not too many know of my relations with Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: But you've been meeting me often lately. Some people have started to notice already.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: So if necessary, we can have a falling-out take place between us.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Would you rather I bring the danger upon Rhodes Island and the Doctor, then?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Hence why I make this choice.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Not to mention...

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: The Druids' legends, the stories of and about life, have been forgotten for far too long.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: They need to be told anew by people.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: You know that kid's never going to find any so-called treasure.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Who told you there was no treasure?

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: You did?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Because you're not a Druid, see.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Only Druids will find the Druid's Treasure.

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: Eh?

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Bitter Root
steps.text: So that little ritual you did before with the incantation or whatever, that was all real?

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: Oh... well, not that, I made that up.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: I just haven't found any of the historical files or data yet, that's the bare minimum of it.

steps.name: Quercus
steps.text: You weren't really taken in by that, were you?
